hypothesis: canonical serialization + packed encoding for binary .atlas (P2)
blocking_question: which items of the canonicalization / untrusted-reader checklist are not already stated by ATLAS-BINARY-WIRE-FORMAT.md and ATLASX-BINARY-WIRE-FORMAT.md?

measurement.method: clause-by-clause comparison against the contracts, executed against the G64/G68 reader and writer and their tests rather than on paper
measurement.byte_for_byte_canonical_form: stated (minimal LEB128 varints, ascending field tags, canonical record and directory order, deterministic publication) and enforced: the reader rejects non-minimal, truncated, overlong and trailing varints (uvarints_are_minimal_bounded_and_exact), non-canonical record and directory order, and undeclared schema identities; the writer refuses non-canonical content; decode-then-re-encode is byte-identical (a_census_container_round_trips_exactly_and_deterministically)
measurement.unstated_item: unknown optional fields: the reader skips them for forward compatibility (field_framing_skips_unknown_optional_fields_and_rejects_unknown_required_ones), and the root identity is the hash of the manifest, which commits to section bytes -- so a container carrying one decodes to the same content as its canonical encoding under a different root. No contract said what SEALED publication does with them
measurement.optimizations_checked_against_canonical_: no packing or compression exists in wire v1; the compression clause (deterministic, or identity over decoded canonical content) already covers the first one
measurement.untrusted_reader_limits: Cap'n Proto's traversal-limit and pointer-amplification concerns are specific to pointer-based formats; .atlas records are flat and length-delimited, and every single-byte corruption and every truncation/extension is rejected (every_single_byte_corruption_is_rejected, every_truncation_and_extension_is_rejected)

decision.contract_amendment: ATLAS-BINARY-WIRE-FORMAT.md, canonical publication: a SEALED encoder must not emit undeclared fields and a SEALED-verifying reader must reject them; unsealed containers may carry them with physical-byte identity. Code waits for the seal gate (exit criterion E)
REFERENCE_ONLY: segment/pointer wire format, packing, schema compiler, RPC (the .atlas wire is flat and length-delimited; no packing in v1)

extinction.test_dependency: none (no code or test references the checkout; not a DC1 Cargo donor)
